newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Authority plans over $1.2 bln of bond sales.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Authority plans over $1.2 bln of bond sales.

text.p: The New York State Dormitory Authority on Thursday said that it plans to sell more than $1.2 billion of bonds in October and November.

The first sale, a $910 million offering of seven-year fixed and variable rate bonds, is expected to be sold on October 30. The negotiated sale, which will be led by Lehman Brothers, will pay the remaining pension fund liability in the Common Retirement Fund.

The second largest sale is a $281 million offering of 25-year, fixed-rate bonds, which is scheduled for November 19. The syndicate, which will be led by Bear, Stearns, will raise $28 million of new money. The rest of the bond proceeds will be used for a refunding, which is projected to save $12.2 million on a present value basis.

The Dormitory Authority also plans to sell on November 14 approximately $23 million of 25-year fixed rated bonds to refund the 1991 Veterans Home Revenue bonds. The sale, which the Authority said it hoped would produce a present value savings of $1 million, will be led by M.R. Beal & Co.

As much as $22 million of 1989 bonds will be refunded in an offering planned for November 13, which also will be led by M.R. Beal & Co. The new 23-year, fixed-rate bonds are expected to save $900,000 on a present value basis.
